title: Homemade Fresh Pasta
description: Nothing beats the taste and texture of fresh, homemade pasta. Simpler than you think and absolutely worth the effort.
instructions: Mound the flour on a clean work surface and create a well in the center. Crack the eggs into the well and add the olive oil and salt.
Using a fork, gently beat the eggs while gradually incorporating flour from the inner edges of the well. Continue until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should bounce back when poked. If it's too sticky, add a little more flour.
Wrap the dough tightly in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. This relaxes the gluten and makes rolling easier.
Divide the rested dough into 4 equal pieces. Keep unused portions covered to prevent drying.
Using a pasta machine or rolling pin, roll each piece into thin sheets. For fettuccine, roll to about 1/16 inch thick.
Dust the sheets lightly with semolina flour, then cut into your desired shape — fettuccine, tagliatelle, or pappardelle.
To cook, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Fresh pasta cooks quickly — only 2-3 minutes! It's done when it floats to the top.
Drain and toss immediately with your favorite sauce. Fresh pasta absorbs sauce beautifully.
notes: The dough can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours or frozen for up to a month. Let it come to room temperature before rolling. For colored pasta, add 2 tbsp tomato paste (red), 2 tbsp spinach puree (green), or 1 tbsp squid ink (black) to the eggs.
